title: Cabbage Roll Casserole
subtitle: all the flavour of Baba's cabbage rolls with none of the rolling: beef, rice and cabbage baked in a sweet-tangy tomato sauce
imageAlt: A scoop of cabbage roll casserole with tender cabbage, beef and rice in red tomato sauce in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: a 9×13 pan: dinner for two, plus 4 lunches

breakdown: Brown sugar, vinegar, garlic, spices, salt

beforeYouStart.text: It bakes 1½ hours, so start early; it reheats even better the next day.

items.name: small head green cabbage
items.note: about 1 kg, cored and cut in 3 cm pieces

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Cook the beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, 8 minutes, until browned with no pink left. Add the garlic for 1 minute. Spoon off the fat; the beef finishes cooking to 74°C (165°F) in the oven.

steps.title: Add the rice
steps.text: Stir the rinsed uncooked rice, paprika, salt and pepper into the beef.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Whisk the tomato sauce, water, brown sugar and vinegar together.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: In a greased 23×33 cm (9×13 in) baking dish, spread half the cabbage, then all the beef and rice, then the rest of the cabbage. Pour the sauce evenly over and press the cabbage down.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Cover tightly with foil and bake 75 minutes. Uncover, press down again and bake 15 minutes more, until the rice and cabbage are tender and the centre reads 74°C (165°F).

fixIt.fix: Stir in ½ cup hot water, cover again and bake 15 minutes more.
Bake uncovered 10–15 minutes more; it also thickens as it rests.
Stir in another tablespoon of brown sugar; tomato sauces vary.

saleTip: Cabbage is one of the cheapest vegetables at No Frills, often under $1/lb; one small head is enough.
swap: Half ground pork, half beef, like many Ukrainian and Polish family recipes; the pork also to 71°C (160°F).
leftovers: Like cabbage rolls, it's better the next day. Pack with a spoon of sour cream.
doneness: Ground beef to 71°C (160°F) (Health Canada, ground beef); bake until the centre reads 74°C (165°F) so the rice and sauce are hot through.
source: Based on tested unrolled (lazy) cabbage roll casserole methods (Canadian Living, Allrecipes): browned beef with uncooked rice layered with chopped cabbage and a sweet-sour tomato sauce, baked covered about 1½ hours.
prepAhead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead and chill; add 15 minutes to the covered bake.
reheat: Covered in the microwave 3 minutes, stirring halfway, or covered at 180°C (350°F) for 25 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Beef, rice, cabbage and tomato sauce; no garlic or paprika.

fancy.note: Crisp bacon on top and a dollop of sour cream, the Ukrainian way.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: first cook the bacon in the skillet until crisp; set it aside and brown the beef in a little of the fat.

addSteps.title: To serve
addSteps.text: Scatter the bacon over the casserole and serve each scoop with a spoon of sour cream.

plating: Sour cream on top, bacon over that.
Black pepper and a slice of rye bread on the side.

why.0-3: Uncooked rice soaks up the sauce as it bakes, just like the filling of a real cabbage roll.
why.1-4: A spoon of vinegar with the sugar gives the classic sweet-sour sauce.
why.1-0: Chopped cabbage turns silky in the long bake: no blanching or rolling.

funFact: Cabbage rolls, holubtsi in Ukrainian, came to the Prairies with Ukrainian settlers in the 1890s and are a church-supper staple across Canada.
